messages.subject: MRDS
parts:
Hi, 

I am just looking a the tee dataset and mrds model building. I was wondering why "distance" is taken into consideration in the mrmodel? In MRDS analyses we use the MR model to model sightability at the line and the DS model to model decay in detection at further distances from the plane.  So why use distances as a covariate for the MR model?   

For example (page 45 of the document title "Package mrds"):
   xx <- ddf(mrmodel=~glm(formula=~distance*observer), dsmodel=~mcds(key="hn", formula=~sex), data=egdata, method="io", meta.data=list(width=4))  

Thanks, 

Lisa

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] MRDS
parts:
Lisa

The mark-recapture component of the MRDS modelling is a logistic regression fitted to the duplicate detections from independent observers. Because it is a generalisation of a Lincoln-Petersen mark-recapture estimator, it is sensitive to unmodelled heterogeneity; hence all possible sources of variation influencing the probability of duplicate detections need to be included in the models. One of those sources of variation could be distance from the transect--probability of duplicate detection could be influenced by distance from the transect.

Most published MRDS analyses include distance in the MR component in the candidate set.  For example, see the Buckland et al. (2015) book which includes analyses of Antarctic crabeater seals (Sect 5.4.2.1), North Sea minke whales (Sect 5.4.2.2) and Texas songbirds (Sect 5.4.2.3).
